To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the recombination model predicts a transition from a deconfinement signal to a hadronic gas behavior for all observables considered.
the quark recombination scenario is able to explain the lack of experimental evidence for a phase transition between quark-gluon plasma and hadronic matter at RHIC.
the dynamical recombination of quarks and antiquarks into mesons and baryons leads to a disappearance of the predicted signals for a quark-gluon plasma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay of microscopic and macroscopic properties of the quark–glun plasma and the hadronic matter.
the interplay between the dynamical evolution of the QCD medium and its hadronization mechanism.
the question whether the microscopic structure of a QCD-matter system can be probed with the help of event-by-event fluctuations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, if a deconfined state is created at RHIC, the hadronization of the quarks into baryons and mesons takes place on a time scale that is comparable to the lifetime of the plasma.
the recombination model is not able to reproduce the observed event-by-event observability of a QCD phase transition at RHIC.
the recombination mechanism is not only a promising approach to describe the hadron formation process but also a very powerful tool to study the properties of the QCD matter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a dynamical parton recombination model is in principle able to explain why the experimental results do not show a clear signature for the deconfinement transition.
a dynamical quasiparticle model is not only able to reproduce all experimental results, but also to explain why the expected signatures of deconfinement have never been found in the data.

the dynamical recombination model predicts that the QGP–hadronization transition is a very smooth process and therefore it is not possible to distinguish the two phases by fluctuation observables alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quark recombination mechanism has to be taken into account when studying the microscopic properties of the QGP created in high-energy heavy-ion collisions.
the quark recombination mechanism is a very efficient process in the early stage of the evolution of the QCD matter created in heavy ion collisions.
the quark–glukon plasma phase of the fireball created at RHIC is not accessible by any of the proposed event-by-event fluctuation observables.
